title: ULearning1
summary: My first game
description: This is my first game made with Unreal Engine. It's a third-person PvE game where you can break things and kill creatures, although this project was mostly to understand how Unreal works, so it isn't a complete fine-tuned game.

body.text: I made a simple start menu to launch the actual game. The goal is to kill the wolf in the dungeon. You can pick up several items like swords, gold, souls and hearts, which affect your health. Gold and souls currently have no use besides the high score.

Each heart color has a different effect, which can be tweaked in the editor, so two hearts of the same color may affect your health by different values. Red ones increase your current health (add 20 or more). Green ones increase your max health. Yellow ones increase both current and max health. Finally, purple ones set your current health to a value, which could be 1 or 1000 depending on your luck :)
I used animation blend spaces and motion warping for enemy attacks, so dodging must be done at the right moment. There are 3 types of enemies: paladins, insects and the wolf.
On a side note, I also experimented with foot inverse kinematics using a sphere trace.

title: ULearning2
summary: My first multiplayer game
description: This is my first multiplayer game made with Unreal Engine. It's a third-person shooter where you must kill your friends and capture points. This project was made to understand how Unreal's Online Subsystem works.

body.text: This project is still ongoing and the repository is private for now, but I'll make it public eventually.

I'm making a simple multiplayer plugin able to create Steam sessions and join them, which I can then reuse in future projects. I've been learning how Unreal's replication system works, even though it's not always clear what is already replicated by default. I've learned how to use rep notifies in C++ along with RPCs to call functions on the server from a client.

title: Infectious Engine
summary: My own game engine project
description: This is my own game engine project. After building a game engine for a university project, I decided to rebuild it from scratch, without the university's time constraints, to make something cleaner.

body.text: This project was my main project until recently. I aimed for a game engine written in C++ using both the OpenGL and Vulkan rendering APIs. The engine would then support a special game using an EEG headset for input (basically controlling the player with your mind!). As an optional challenge, I would then rewrite the engine in Rust to learn this interesting language.

Unfortunately, I had to choose between focusing on the Engine Programmer or the Gameplay Programmer path, and I always wanted to be in gameplay, so this project is currently on hiatus until I'm done learning Unreal Engine (and have found a job 😉).

title: Snow Temple Run
summary: Our own game engine and game project made during university
description: This is a university project I worked on with 2 of my classmates, where the goal was to create a game engine and a game using this same engine.

body.text: To do this, we used Qt (C++) and OpenGL as the graphics API. We chose to take the mobile game Temple Run and give it a winter theme with a snowman. We also challenged ourselves to move only the background and obstacles, not the character. It's an endless game where the goal is to get the best score possible by avoiding ice cubes.

The three snowballs of the snowman represent the number of remaining lives, each obstacle removing one life. However, it is still possible to recover a snowball that falls from the walls when only one life is left.
In this project, I was mainly involved in setting up the collision detection system and the texture and lighting system, and I participated in designing the engine's scene graph architecture.

title: ARPA
summary: Augmented Reality Piano Assistant
description: ARPA (Augmented Reality Piano Assistant) is a university project I worked on with 2 of my classmates, using Unity and a Leap Motion to detect the user's hands.

body.text: With certain hand movements, you can zoom in/out on the piano or move along it. With the help of different techniques, such as quantization, we were able to reduce sensor imprecision and thus accidental errors, such as double taps. It is also possible to visualize which chords are being played. Here are some demonstration videos of the final application (in French).

title: Anime List
summary: Windows application to list all series/anime you watched or want to watch
description: This is an application listing various series/anime with various statistics.

body.text: I created an application using JavaScript and the front-end frameworks React and Electron: a Windows application able to list series watched or to be watched, as well as available languages, release dates and other information. Initially, this application was intended for a friend, but it will eventually be usable by everyone.
A customization tab has been added to change the colors as desired and the main theme (dark or light).

body.alt: Screenshot of the theme and color settings

body.text: The goal was to discover and understand how rendering a simple scene works with OpenGL, through the freeCodeCamp tutorial. I later wanted to use it as a base for various exercises or projects without having to rewrite the basics every time.

title: Inpainting
summary: University project: an image reconstruction application
description: This is a university project consisting of an application that performs image reconstruction, made with a classmate.

body.text: Our aim was to develop an application that can take an image as input and let the user select areas to be repainted, in order to reconstruct or erase elements of the image.

Our initial approach was to calculate the average of the surrounding pixels. We also discovered another method called Fast Marching Method (FMM) that promises significantly better results while remaining performant, but we didn't have time to implement it. To select an area to paint, just click on a pixel of the image and change the sensitivity (the color variance detection) using the mouse wheel.

title: Image HDR
summary: University project: HDR images for astrophotography
description: This is a university project: an application that generates high dynamic range (HDR) images for astrophotography, made with a classmate.

body.text: Our project was to create an application that could take in a night sky image as input and apply different HDR algorithms to enhance it.
We used Qt to create an easy-to-use interface, and we implemented different HDR algorithms using OpenCV, such as those of Robertson, Debevec and Mertens.

body.alt: Poster explaining how the HDR application works

body.text: We also tested several noise reduction methods, a common problem in astrophotography, first by averaging the images and then using a convolutional neural network.

Finally, our results were quite satisfactory and we were able to develop an application that offered different options for tone mapping and HDR algorithms to produce an enhanced image. Here is the final poster that explains how we made the application (in French).

body.alt: Final poster explaining how the HDR application works

title: Maze Algorithms
summary: Two maze generation algorithms, written with p5.js
description: This is a simple project consisting of two different maze generation algorithms.

body.text: This is a small program written with the p5.js framework that generates a maze, the goal being to experiment with different algorithms, including one using backtracking and another using recursive division of space.

title: Accessible CMS
summary: R&D for programming a CMS that produces websites respecting accessibility criteria
description: This is a database project listing all web accessibility criteria.

body.text: During my final internship, I developed a project aimed at preparing the development of a CMS that produces accessible websites.

To do this, I created an application with a database that includes all the accessibility criteria from WCAG, and an API that will allow this future CMS to request validations or recommendations regarding the user's ongoing production.
This project showed me how important accessibility is on the web as well as in video games. Unfortunately, due to the nature of the project, I cannot show anything here.

title: Portfolio 3D
summary: 3D version of this portfolio
description: This is this portfolio, but made with Three.js and React.

body.text: It's basically the same portfolio with more interactivity. I will embed some games that I will make in the future in the scene.
It's also currently available in both French and English, whereas this portfolio is English only.

It's made of two scenes. The default one is a room with some clickable elements that trigger cinematics, games or events. The other scene is the projects scene, where you can find my projects in space around planet Earth.
You can scroll down in the default scene to see the about, contact and CV pages, or just navigate with the navbar.
